thread.title_full: Six days out, severe weather highlighted for St. Louis region to begin next week - NewsBreak

author: Brendan Sanders
title: Six days out, severe weather highlighted for St. Louis region to begin next week - NewsBreak
text:
By Brendan Sanders ,
7 hours ago Severe weather is currently expected up to St. Louis on Tuesday. (NOAA Storm Prediction Center) Though it is several days away, an active period of severe weather is expected over the next week, and storms are possible in the Mississippi Valley region by early next week.
The NOAA Storm Prediction Center has highlighted severe weather chances for areas around the St. Louis area six days out, as a volatile weather system is set to pass over the Central United States.
A 15% severe weather risk has been highlighted in the Eastern Missouri region, reaching to the St. Louis area and the Mississippi River Valley for both Monday, April 13 and Tuesday, April 14.
Severe weather is currently expected just west of St. Louis on Monday. (NOAA Storm Prediction Center) The Monday threat is currently expected a bit further west, staying just west of Washington, Missouri. This is part of a system that is currently projected to stretch from Central Texas all the way to Wisconsin as a moist and unstable airmass is forecast to remain from the southern Plains extending northeastward into the Upper Midwest.
Severe weather stretches across the Great Plains on Monday, April 13. (NOAA Storm Prediction Center) “Strong to severe thunderstorm development will be possible over much of the instability corridor in the afternoon and evening,” the Storm Prediction Center said. “The greatest potential for severe storms is forecast from the southern Plains north northeastward into the lower Missouri Valley and upper Mississippi Valley, where the models develop moderate instability and have 0-6 km shear mostly in the 30 to 40 knot range. Severe storms with large hail, wind damage and a tornado threat will be possible.”
Tuesday will bring another round of severe storms to the region, with St. Louis sitting on the northern edge of the risk area that expands south through Arkansas, Eastern Oklahoma and Texas. The SPC notes that the western U.S. trough is finally forecast to approach the southern Plains on Tuesday, where a moist and unstable airmass should be in place.
Severe weather stretches up to St. Louis on Tuesday, April 14. (NOAA Storm Prediction Center) “Some solutions suggest that a mid-level jet will move into the southern Plains Tuesday afternoon,” the Storm Prediction Center said. “This would create strong, deep-layer shear over parts of the moist sector, suggesting that a substantial severe threat will be possible. Although there is still spatial uncertainty regarding this scenario, current model forecasts would support supercells with large hail, severe wind gusts and some tornadoes.”
Now, this is still several days out, so there is plenty of time for the severe weather threats to change, diminish, or shift, as this will be part of an active weather period that will begin on Saturday, April 11 and run for multiple days. Thus, more updates will come as the forecast period draws near.
“The key takeaway here is that given the time range (5+ days), many uncertainties remain with respect to severe weather potential, but it is important to note that the signal is there for severe weather at the start of next week,” the St. Louis NWS said .
